glm.title: General Linear Model
glm.boxM: Box's Test of Equality of Covariance Matrices
glm.boxNote: Tests the null hypothesis that the observed covariance matrices of the dependent variables are equal across groups.
glm.boxNone: Box's M is not computed: fewer than two groups have nonsingular covariance matrices.
glm.upperBound: The statistic is an upper bound on F that yields a lower bound on the significance level.
glm.mvSingular: Multivariate tests cannot be computed: the error SSCP matrix is singular or there are too few residual degrees of freedom.
glm.mauchlyNote: Tests the null hypothesis that the error covariance matrix of the orthonormalized transformed dependent variables is proportional to an identity matrix.
glm.epsilonNote: May be used to adjust the degrees of freedom for the averaged tests of significance. Corrected tests are displayed in the Tests of Within-Subjects Effects table.
glm.levene: Levene's Test of Equality of Error Variances
glm.leveneNote: Tests the null hypothesis that the error variance of the dependent variable is equal across groups.
glm.redundant: This parameter is set to zero because it is redundant.
glm.diffSig: The mean difference is significant at the {{alpha}} level.
glm.adjLsd: Adjustment for multiple comparisons: Least Significant Difference (equivalent to no adjustments).
glm.covAt: Covariates appearing in the model are evaluated at the following values: {{list}}.
glm.notEstimable: This level combination of factors is not observed, thus the corresponding population marginal mean is not estimable.
glm.noValid: There are no valid cases for this analysis.
glm.dfE0: There are no residual degrees of freedom; the tests cannot be computed.
glm.plotSkipped: Profile plots (PLOT) are not drawn; use the estimated marginal means instead.
glm.keywordIgnored: PRINT={{keyword}} is not supported and was ignored.
glm.subIgnored: The {{sub}} subcommand is not supported for multivariate and repeated measures GLM and was ignored.

glmRepeated.title: General linear model (repeated measures)
glmRepeated.levels2: Number of levels of the second factor
glmRepeated.measuresHint: One row per level, in order; with two factors the second factor changes fastest (1,1  1,2 … 2,1 …).
glmRepeated.needName: Enter a name for the within-subjects factor.
glmRepeated.badName: The factor name must be a valid name (letters, digits, _) that is not a variable name.
glmRepeated.rowCount: The number of within-subjects variables must equal the number of levels (product of the levels for two factors).
glmRepeated.fillAll: Choose a variable for every level (each variable once).
glmRepeated.rowsHint: {{count}} within-subjects variables are needed for the levels defined.
